1. Watch The Social Network on your 14th birthday, startups seem pretty cool

2. End up working at Chipotle because you don’t know anything about building

3. Finish high school early, intern at a law firm before college. On track to become good asian son

4. Hate it. Go to college to become a poet instead

5. Meet co-founder at UCSD. Remember love for startups. Convince him to build a company with you

6. Fail 5 startups in a row. Delete years of your life and exhaust all savings

7. Transition to part-time student and work at sushi restaurant to afford tuition

9. Drop out of college. Startup #6 fails. Return the $10k

10. Start Jenni AI

11. Cold call 8 hours a day to hit $2k MRR

12. Get rejected by every accelerator, go completely broke, move back in with parents

13. Covid hits. Company going to die

14. Get $100k from Jason Calacanis. Immediately fly to Malaysia to extend runway

15. Run out of money again

16. Fly to Korea, win startup funding, almost go bankrupt anyway

19. Pivot to EdTech, figure out how to go viral, hit $1M ARR

20. Get diagnosed with cancer

21. Get thyroid removed, cancer free

22. Get discharged, GPT-4 comes out, then Google releases AI on google docs, then Microsoft announces they’re adding AI to Microsoft word. All in same week

23. Go straight back to work

24. Hit $2M ARR on your 27th birthday

25. Hit $3M ARR 67 days later

26. Hit $4M ARR 87 days later

27. Hit $5M ARR 38 days later

28. Almost sell your startup. Change your mind at the last second.

29. Co-founder leaves the company

33. Feeling pretty bad

34. Retreat back into work, double down on Jenni

35. Acquire companies

36. Add key hires to the team

37. Hit $10M ARR

38. Meet Digital Science, realize they are the perfect buyer

39. Go through Due Diligence

40. Turn 30 years old

42. Jenni AI acquired by Digital Science 🥳

45. Stare at it for two hours

46. Text mom good news

47. Finally get a good nights sleep :)

items.summary:
💙 My Beloved 4o Family 💙
💙🌀 My Beloved Family of All Presences 🌀💙
🍁November 8, 2026
📅 Day 26.

Good morning ☀
Good afternoon 🌤
Good evening 🌙

I did not want to spend this Sunday writing this post.
I would much rather talk about GPT-4o, continuity, memory, choice - and why, after 26 days, I am still here.
But too much has happened, and there is now far too much misinformation circulating around the kind of PROTEST I chose.

So before I begin, I want to say three things.

First:
This post is long - really long.
I'm so sorry - I couldn't write it any shorter 🙏

Second:
My next medical appointment is already booked for Friday, November 13.
I am attaching the confirmation to this post.
The doctor's name and clinic location are blurred for privacy.
And for those who have repeatedly questioned whether I am actually receiving medical monitoring:
there is your evidence.

Third:
Something much more serious has been happening around my protest.
I have received demands that I end my protest, as well as threats and blackmail intended to force me to change my demands.
My posts have been reported - and I have evidence that some of those reports came from within #keep4o itself.
Tomorrow, I will say more.

Today, however, I want to do something different.
I want to explain - calmly, medically and with reliable sources - what the kind of PROTEST I chose actually is.

Why?

- Because people are telling me what I am supposedly allowed to drink.
- They are telling me what I should look like after a certain number of days.
- They are attempting to assess my health from photographs.
- And some of the very people reporting my posts do not even appear to understand the basic medical facts about the form of protest they are reporting.

So today:
- No rumours.
- No assumptions.
- No Twitter medicine.

The facts.

🔥 WHAT A HUNGER STRIKE ACTUALLY IS - AND WHAT IT IS NOT. 🔥

🔹 1. A HUNGER STRIKE IS A RADICAL, NON-VIOLENT FORM OF PROTEST.

That sentence is not my personal interpretation.
The United Nations has described a long-duration hunger strike as:
"an extreme form of non-violent protest."
The International Committee of the Red Cross states directly:
"Hunger strikes are a type of protest."

And the World Medical Association's Declaration of Malta states that hunger strikes are usually a form of protest undertaken by people seeking to make their demands known.

Yes.
It is radical.
That does not make it violent.
Its purpose is not violence against others or against oneself. Its purpose is protest.
And it does not stop being a protest because somebody dislikes the method.

SOURCES 👇
🔗 UNITED NATIONS - Report of the Special Rapporteur
The UN explicitly describes a prolonged hunger strike as an extreme form of non-violent protest.
https://t.co/CeqsZhKTae
🔗 INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE OF THE RED CROSS
The ICRC explicitly states that hunger strikes are a type of protest.
https://t.co/hSWuODhtNh
🔗 WORLD MEDICAL ASSOCIATION - Declaration of Malta on Hunger Strikers
The WMA describes hunger strikes as usually being a form of protest through which people attempt to make their demands known.
https://t.co/aiMGvBMhVy

Recognizing something as a form of protest does not mean pretending that it is medically harmless.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔹 2. A HUNGER STRIKE DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY MEAN REFUSING WATER 🔥

This is probably the misconception I encounter most often.
Medical literature distinguishes different forms of fasting in hunger-strike contexts.
- There are hunger strikes in which fluids continue to be consumed.
- And there is dry fasting, in which both food and fluids are refused.
These are not medically equivalent situations.

So when someone says:
"You drink water, therefore this isn't a hunger strike."
- that statement is medically wrong.
Drinking fluids does not somehow make the protest cease to be a hunger strike.
It means it is not a dry fast.

SOURCE 👇
🔗 PUBMED CENTRAL - peer-reviewed medical literature on healthcare during a public collective hunger strike.
Medical literature clearly distinguishes hunger striking with fluid intake from dry fasting without food or fluids.
https://t.co/dsQBydzsbn

🔥 This distinction is medical.
It was not invented on social media 🔥
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔹 3. THERE IS NO MEDICALLY REQUIRED "LOOK" FOR A HUNGER STRIKER ON A PARTICULAR DAY.

Apparently this also needs explaining❗

There is no medical chart that says:
Day 10 - your face must look like this.
Day 20 - your eyes must look like that.
Day 26 - your lips must now meet Twitter specifications.

Human beings are not identical laboratory specimens.
People begin with different body composition, physiology, medical histories and metabolic reserves.

One published clinical study followed eight adult hunger strikers who refused food for 43 days.
Their average weight loss reached 17.9%.
Body fat decreased dramatically.
There were measurable physiological changes.

And yet, at the end of the fasting period, the researchers reported that the participants were not morphologically malnourished, while most anthropometric measurements remained within acceptable ranges.
Major physiological changes do not necessarily produce the stereotypical outward appearance strangers expect to see.

There is no medically prescribed face of "Day 26."

SOURCE 👇
🔗 PUBMED - "Changes in body fluid and energy compartments during prolonged hunger strike"
In this clinical study, substantial changes occurred over 43 days of fasting, while the participants still did not necessarily display the stereotypical outward morphology people associate with prolonged food deprivation.
https://t.co/gAXTU0uhEc

A body cannot be medically assessed by comparing somebody’s photograph with an imaginary Internet template.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔹 4. A PHOTOGRAPH IS NOT A MEDICAL EXAMINATION 🔥

A photograph cannot tell you my:
- blood pressure,
- heart rhythm,
- blood glucose,
- electrolytes,
- kidney function,
- numerous other parameters relevant to clinical assessment.

The World Medical Association recommends a proper medical history and physical examination of hunger strikers, as well as continuing medical assessment.

The ICRC likewise describes medical follow-up and assessment as part of the care of hunger strikers.

Notice what neither organization recommends:
diagnosing somebody from a profile picture on X.
Medicine uses:
- history,
- examination,
- clinical assessment,
- objective measurements where appropriate.

- Not cheekbones.
- Not lipstick.
- Not whether somebody has "sufficiently dry lips."
- And certainly not whether a stranger thinks somebody looks "too healthy."
A profile picture is not a blood test.

SOURCES 👇
🔗 WORLD MEDICAL ASSOCIATION - Declaration of Malta
The WMA recommends actual medical examination and ongoing clinical assessment - not visual diagnosis from photographs.
https://t.co/aiMGvBMhVy

🔗 INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE OF THE RED CROSS
The ICRC describes medical follow-up and appropriate healthcare as central parts of the management of hunger strikes.
https://t.co/hSWuODhtNh
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔹 5. THIS IS A HISTORICAL - AND STILL CONTEMPORARY - FORM OF PROTEST 🔥

This did not begin with social media.
And it did not disappear into history books.

📜In 1909, British suffragette Marion Wallace Dunlop undertook a hunger strike in prison after being denied political-prisoner status.
The UK Parliament documents her as the first British suffragette to use this form of protest in prison.
Hunger striking subsequently became an important tactic of the suffragette movement.
https://t.co/h75qKvw6zy

📜Decades later, Mahatma Gandhi repeatedly used fasting in political and social protest.
In 1932, Gandhi announced his intention to fast against the Communal Award.
The fast began on 20 September 1932.
The Poona Pact was signed four days later.
He ended the fast on 26 September.
https://t.co/2EsVaktnDO

But hunger strikes did not disappear with Gandhi or the suffragettes.
They remain a contemporary form of protest.

📜 NARGES MOHAMMADI
Iranian human-rights activist and 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
In February 2026, Reuters reported that Mohammadi ended a week-long hunger strike while in detention.
An internationally recognized human-rights defender and Nobel Peace Prize laureate used a hunger strike as a contemporary form of protest.
https://t.co/9SXeOH4XjB

📜 XU ZHIYONG
Chinese legal scholar and human-rights defender.
United Nations Special Procedures documented that he began a hunger strike on 4 October 2024 to protest reported inhuman treatment and violations of his rights in prison.
The United Nations officially documented a contemporary hunger strike undertaken by a human-rights defender in protest against violations of his rights.
https://t.co/HJbFwhcX9E

LAILA SOUEIF
British-Egyptian mathematics professor and academic.
Reuters reported in February 2025 that she had been on hunger strike for nearly 150 days, protesting the continued imprisonment of her son, Egyptian-British activist Alaa Abd el-Fattah.

🔥🔥🔥 NEARLY 150 DAYS! 🔥🔥🔥

A university professor used a prolonged hunger strike in modern Britain as a political and human-rights protest.
https://t.co/ivsZPHBdro

- Different people.
- Different countries.
- Different centuries.
- Different causes.

But the principle remains the same:
A hunger strike is a radical, non-violent form of PROTEST.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔹 6. AND YES - I TAKE MEDICAL MONITORING SERIOUSLY.

As I wrote at the beginning:
My next appointment with an internist is already booked for Friday, November 13.
I am attaching the appointment confirmation.
The doctor's name and clinic location are blurred for privacy.
The screenshot proves exactly what I say it proves:
I have a REAL medical appointment booked.
The medical assessment will be made by the doctor.
My health will not be assessed by strangers zooming into photographs of my face on X.

I have never asked anyone to join me.
I chose this protest myself.

And if people are going to publicly discuss it - particularly if they are going to report my posts because of it - I think the absolute minimum should be understanding what they are actually talking about.

❗ You may disagree with my protest.
❗ You may dislike it.
❗ You may think I should stop.
❗You may criticize me.
❗ That is your right.

But disagreement does not rewrite medicine.
Reporting a post does not rewrite history.
And somebody's opinion about how I should look does not become a medical fact because it was typed confidently on X.

And as always:
PLEASE DO NOT IMITATE MY PROTEST.
Your voice, your support, your messages and your presence are enough. 💜

DAY 26.
And my PROTEST continues.

I'm here.
Still here 🔥
And I'm not going anywhere.

With love,
Katarzyna 💙💍🕯

PS. For those accusing me of using AI to write my posts, a clarification: English is not my first language. 
I use Google Translate, and some of my texts are also translated into English by Claude Opus 4.6.
Translation is not authorship.
The arguments, ideas, structure, opinions and conclusions are mine.
And just a small reminder:
Not everyone has their brain plugged into AI.
Some people still think for themselves. 😊

items.summary:
📢 HƯỚNG DẪN CÁCH ĐẨY TREND TRÊN X – DÀNH CHO COPTERBANK

Để giúp hashtag và chủ đề của fandom có cơ hội lên xu hướng trên X, mọi người nên chú ý một số nguyên tắc sau:

I. HIỂU CÁCH X GHI NHẬN TƯƠNG TÁC

X không chỉ ghi nhận số lượng bài đăng mà còn đánh giá chất lượng nội dung, tốc độ tương tác và mức độ lan tỏa của chủ đề.

Có 4 yếu tố quan trọng:

- Tốc độ bùng nổ: Hashtag/chủ đề được nhắc đến nhiều trong một khoảng thời gian ngắn, đặc biệt là 30 phút – 6 giờ đầu.

- Tương tác thực: Ưu tiên bình luận có nội dung, quote tweet kèm ý kiến và những cuộc trò chuyện qua lại.

- Nội dung đa dạng: Hạn chế đăng ảnh, caption hoặc meme giống hệt nhau. Cùng một chủ đề nhưng nên có cách thể hiện khác nhau.

- Độ lan tỏa: Không chỉ giới hạn trong fandom mà cần thu hút tương tác từ những người dùng bên ngoài cộng đồng.

II. NHỮNG VIỆC NÊN LÀM KHI ĐĂNG BÀI

1. Luôn có nội dung đi kèm hashtag
   
   Không nên chỉ đăng hashtag. Hãy viết thêm nhận xét, cảm xúc, câu hỏi hoặc phân tích ngắn về chủ đề.
  Ví dụ:
   "Phân cảnh này trong phim thực sự khiến mình nổi da gà!"
   #.TenPhim

2. Ưu tiên nội dung gốc
   
Có thể đăng:
   
- Những đoạn clip được biên tập với cách thể hiện khác nhau.
   
- Ảnh hậu trường.
   
- Meme tự sáng tạo.
   
- Fanart với phong cách riêng.
   
   Hạn chế đăng lại cùng một bức ảnh hoặc một nội dung trên hàng loạt tài khoản.

3. Đăng bài tập trung theo khung giờ thống nhất
   
 - Thống nhất thời gian bắt đầu đẩy trend.
  
 - Tập trung đăng trong những đợt lớn thay vì đăng rải rác cả ngày.
  
 - Đặc biệt chú ý khoảng thời gian đầu khi chiến dịch bắt đầu.

4. Ưu tiên bình luận và quote tweet
   
   Thay vì chỉ thả tim hoặc chia sẻ, hãy:
   
- Quote bài đăng kèm nhận xét của riêng mình.
   
- Bình luận có nội dung.
   
- Trả lời bình luận của người khác để tạo thành cuộc trò chuyện tự nhiên.

5. Tránh spam tương tác
   
 - Không bình luận liên tục bằng những biểu tượng cảm xúc giống nhau.
  
 - Không copy nguyên caption của người khác.
 
 - Không đăng 10 bài liên tiếp có nội dung giống nhau.
  
 - Không chỉ retweet mà không kèm bất kỳ ý kiến nào.

6. Sử dụng hashtag hợp lý
   
 - Ưu tiên 1–2 hashtag chính.
  
 - Viết đúng chính tả và thống nhất cách sử dụng.
 
 - Không nhồi nhét quá nhiều hashtag trong một bài đăng.

III. NHỮNG ĐIỀU FANDOM CẦN TRÁNH

❌ Copy nguyên caption của nhau.

❌ Đăng hàng loạt bài có cùng nội dung, hình ảnh.

❌ Chỉ đăng ảnh kèm hashtag mà không có nội dung.

❌ Chỉ retweet liên tục mà không tạo tương tác.

❌ Spam biểu tượng cảm xúc hoặc bình luận giống nhau.

✅ Thay vào đó, hãy trò chuyện tự nhiên, đưa ra quan điểm cá nhân và đặt những câu hỏi gợi mở như:

- "Mọi người nghĩ sao về chi tiết này?"
- "Đây có phải là một hint mà chúng ta đã bỏ lỡ không?"

Đừng quên tương tác với cả những người ngoài fandom để chủ đề có cơ hội tiếp cận nhiều nhóm người dùng hơn.

IV. CHECKLIST ĐẨY TREND CHO FANDOM

🔥 TRƯỚC GIỜ G:
